newsitem.title: USA: Wired takes new stab at IPO in stronger market.
newsitem.headline: Wired takes new stab at IPO in stronger market.

text.p: Wired Ventures Inc, the publisher of Wired magazine, will again try to go public, but its initial public offering could have a much different reception this time around in a market hot for tech stocks and IPOs.

The company said it filed a revised registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for an offering of up to 4,750,000 shares to price in a range of $12 to $14 a share. The deal is expected to be completed in October, the company said in a statement.

Wired filed to go public at the end of May but pulled the plug on the deal in July as tech stocks got battered in the broader market. Wired president Jane Metcalfe told employees at the time the company would "wait until the storm has passed" to go public.

"Well, the weather has lifted and the IPOs are sitting on the runway waiting to take off. The industry looks much better so they're running it up the flagpole again," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket publication.
He said even more companies could be expected to "dust off their red herring" and try to come to market, hoping investors would shrug offer summer delays.

Hot Topic Inc was one of the first of the summer postponements to test the market's waters. The company, which makes "retro" wear aimed at teenagers, soared at its initial public offering last week, up 11-1/4 to 29-1/4. It now trades at about 23-1/2.
Stage Stores Inc, DIGEX Inc, Summit Design Inc, and CN Biosciences Inc have also made fresh filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for IPOs.
